assumptions: No web access; analysis based on vendor postures known as of early 2026. Brightline is a 40-person Dublin agency, GDPR-bound, with client PII (contacts, campaign audiences) in scope. Budget-sensitive mid-market buyer with no in-house CRM admin.
gdpr_data_residency: All three vendors offer EU hosting, but with different friction. Salesforce: EU hosting via Hyperforce EU (Frankfurt/Paris); the stricter 'EU Operating Zone' (EU-only support access) is a paid add-on, and Salesforce's US parentage keeps Schrems II / FISA 702 residual transfer risk alive even with SCCs and processor BCRs. HubSpot: EU data residency (AWS Frankfurt) must be selected at portal creation and cannot be changed later without a migration; GDPR tooling (consent capture, cookie banners, deletion workflows) is built in and well suited to an agency handling client marketing data. Zoho: EU data centres in Amsterdam and Dublin, privacy-centric business model (no ad monetisation), strongest residency story on paper, though sub-processor transparency and DPA maturity are less polished than the US incumbents. All three sign DPAs and SCCs. Net: Zoho best raw residency, HubSpot best practical GDPR ergonomics, Salesforce compliant but costliest to lock down.
vendor_lock_in_and_exit: Salesforce is the highest lock-in: proprietary metadata, Apex customisations, AppExchange dependencies, and consultant-built config make exits 6-12 month projects; full data export is possible (weekly export) but schema reconstruction is expensive. HubSpot is moderate: clean CRM export via API/CSV, but workflows, marketing assets, and reporting do not port; effective exit cost for a 40-seat org is roughly 4-8 weeks of effort. Zoho is lowest lock-in (straightforward exports, simpler object model), and annual-only discount terms are short. Contract note: Salesforce contracts auto-renew with uplift clauses and are hard to shrink mid-term; HubSpot and Zoho allow easier seat-count reduction at renewal.
migration_risk: Brightline is assumed to be migrating from spreadsheets/email or a lightweight tool, so data-volume risk is low for all three. Salesforce carries the highest implementation risk: it effectively requires a paid implementation partner, and mid-market Salesforce projects commonly overrun. HubSpot has guided onboarding (mandatory paid onboarding fee) and strong importers; realistic go-live in 4-6 weeks. Zoho migration tooling is adequate but the EU/Irish partner ecosystem is thinner, so internal effort is higher. Ad-ops integration migration (LinkedIn/Meta/Google Ads connectors) is native in HubSpot, marketplace/partner-dependent in Salesforce and Zoho.
hidden_cost_risk: Salesforce: highest — Enterprise-tier features needed for real workflows, ~30% Premier Support uplift, sandbox costs, CPQ/Inbox add-ons, partner fees; realistic TCO often 2-3x sticker. HubSpot: moderate — 'marketing contacts' tier pricing can spike with large client audience lists, Sales/Marketing Hub Pro tiers gate automation, mandatory onboarding fees (~EUR 1,500-3,000); pricing is otherwise transparent. Zoho: lowest sticker risk, but premium support (20-25% of licence) and connector gaps create consultancy or workaround costs.
support_risk: Salesforce standard support is slow without Premier (paid); strong partner network in Dublin mitigates. HubSpot includes phone/email support on Pro tiers with good SLAs and a large EMEA support org. Zoho standard support is the weakest (timezone lag, slower escalation); paid Premium support is near-mandatory for business-critical use.

risk_register.risk: US CLOUD Act / Schrems II transfer exposure despite EU hosting
risk_register.mitigation: Purchase EU Operating Zone add-on; rely on processor BCRs and SCCs; minimise special-category data in CRM.

risk_register.risk: EU data residency must be chosen at portal creation and is hard to change later
risk_register.mitigation: Explicitly provision the portal in the EU (Frankfurt) data centre on day one; verify in account settings before any data import.

risk_register.risk: Deep lock-in via proprietary config and partner-built customisation; exit is a 6-12 month project
risk_register.mitigation: Avoid Apex/custom objects where standard config suffices; document schema; negotiate data-export assistance into the MSA.

risk_register.risk: Implementation overrun and consultant dependency for a 40-seat org with no CRM admin
risk_register.mitigation: Fixed-price implementation contract with milestone payments; pilot with one team before full rollout.

risk_register.risk: Marketing-contacts tier pricing spikes when client audience lists are imported
risk_register.mitigation: Keep client campaign audiences in ad platforms, not the CRM; set non-marketing contact status by default; cap tier in contract.

risk_register.risk: Auto-renewal with price uplift and inability to reduce seats mid-term
risk_register.mitigation: Negotiate renewal price caps and seat-flex clauses before signature; calendar the renewal notice window.

risk_register.risk: Weak standard support and thin Irish partner ecosystem slows incident resolution
risk_register.mitigation: Budget Premium support (20-25% of licence); identify an EU Zoho partner before purchase.

risk_register.risk: Ad-ops connector gaps force custom integration work
risk_register.mitigation: Validate LinkedIn/Meta/Google Ads connectors in trial; budget Zoho Flow/Make middleware.

risk_register.risk: Workflow/asset lock-in grows over time even though contact data exports cleanly
risk_register.mitigation: Keep an exported data dictionary; review automation inventory annually; avoid HubSpot CMS for the agency website.

risk_register.risk: Sub-processor and DPA documentation less mature, complicating client-side GDPR audits
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain signed DPA and sub-processor list pre-contract; map to Art. 28 checklist.

risk_recommendation_rationale: On a pure risk basis Zoho has the cheapest exit and best residency, but its support and integration risks are the most likely to materialise for an ad agency. Salesforce concentrates the highest-severity risks (lock-in, cost overrun) for a 40-person firm. HubSpot, provisioned in the EU data centre with marketing-contact controls contractually capped, offers the lowest aggregate residual risk: moderate lock-in, transparent costs, strong support, native ad-ops integrations. Confidence 4/5; the call would change if Brightline expects to exceed ~50k marketing contacts, which would re-open the Zoho case.
